messages.author: 23f5cfed7a25786f
messages.subject: Problem with big genotype file
parts:
Hey all,

I'm struggling to order a map from a big genotype file (4911 markers and 130 cultivars). The script is running for over a week. This is the code I'm using:

mapthis <- read.cross("csv", getwd(), "rqtl.csv", crosstype = "riself", estimate.map= FALSE)
mapthis <- est.rf(mapthis)
mapthis <- formLinkageGroups(mapthis, max.rf=maxrf, min.lod=minlod, reorgMarkers=TRUE)
mapthis <- orderMarkers(mapthis, map.function = 'haldane', error.prob=0.005)

orderMarkers function is the one taking all this time. I've also tried to run one chromosome / LG at the time with no success. Also tried maxit=10, use.ripple=FALSE, but none of them increased the time / ended in a reasonable time.

Is there something you could think I can do to order this map?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problem with big genotype file
parts:
Order markers when you have a lot, by the method that R/qtl uses, takes
a lot of time.
Start with the linkage group with the fewest markers. How many markers
are on the smallest and largest linkage groups?

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problem with big genotype file
parts:
I would look more closely at why the majority of markers are ending in linkage group 1. It seems to me unlikely that these are really all on the same chromosome.

A common cause for this is apparent segregation distortion at many markers, perhaps as the result of genotyping problems.

Take a look at the results of geno.table(). Are markers segregating 1:1 as expected?

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problem with big genotype file
parts:
Hmm. There doesn't seem to be appreciable segregation distortion.
But you're not explicit on what you used for max.rf and min.lod.
Try using max.rf=0.25 and min.lod=10. You'll end up with more balanced linkage groups.

karl
